title: Asana AI assistant for project handoffs and task reviews
h1: an asana assistant for the work between tasks
description: Connect Asana to Metal for dependency checks, handoff lists and project reviews. Copy three routines and see the actions and limits behind them.
answer: **walk into the handoff knowing what still blocks it.** an asana bot can read tasks, comments, subtasks and dependencies together, then name the unfinished work and its owner. give that review to a Metal bot using the ai you choose. start read only. let the review earn your trust before allowing it to change tasks.
og_line: find the work holding up the handoff.

app.name: Asana
app.intro: **find the missing prerequisite before the launch meeting.** the bot can read the project, comments and dependencies together. these actions get you from "launch ready" to the task still holding it up.

highlight.use: collect the tasks in the launch project for a handoff review
read task comments before calling something blocked
find the unfinished prerequisite holding up tomorrow's handoff
look for unfinished details hidden below a parent task
compare the latest project update with the current task list
find the right section before suggesting a move
turn the next step you agreed on into a task with your details
apply a task correction after you have set the rule for changes

app.setup:
**keep the first project review read only.**

in **connected apps**, allow the project bot to use asana. name the workspace and project, especially when projects share a name.

choose an exact list of allowed actions to keep task creation available. leave unrelated changes out of reach.

routines_intro: **start with a question, not a workspace dump.** name your project and send one of these. findings come back to your dusk chat before you allow task edits.

routines.name: check tomorrow's handoff
routines.message: every afternoon at 3, read tomorrow's tasks in the launch project in asana. read their subtasks and dependencies. list unfinished prerequisites and the person assigned, if assigned. return the checklist here. leave every task date alone. if nothing blocks the handoff, say so in one line.
routines.output: a checklist of unfinished handoff work in your chat

routines.name: compare the status note
routines.message: every monday at 10, read the website project's latest asana status update and current tasks. flag completion claims with unfinished subtasks. name the tasks. separate missing details from actual contradictions. return questions here; don't post a status update.
routines.output: questions for the project owner; no status post

routines.name: prepare a contractor return
routines.message: every thursday at 2, find the named contractor's tasks in the design project in asana. read their comments. list questions still waiting for our answer, grouped by task. return the list here. never reassign tasks or post comments. if none need an answer, say so briefly.
routines.output: a task-by-task reply list for the contractor check-in

asks:
**keep the first review from becoming a reshuffle.** read-only access blocks task creation, edits and section moves before they reach asana.

when you want edits, allow the particular actions and write "ask me before you change anything". due-date changes and reassignments do not automatically wait for an approval card.
cannot: **it cannot see projects your connected account cannot open.** name the exact workspace and project when names overlap.
**it cannot create tasks or correct assignments with read-only access.** these review routines leave records alone.
**it cannot review tomorrow's handoff from a sleeping desktop.** keep the machine awake with dusk open, or use dusk cloud.

sections.md:
**put the unfinished prerequisite beside the claim that launch is ready.** tell the bot what counts as blocked for your team. ask it to show what it found and what it couldn't find.

if delivery also lives in [jira](/integrations/jira), connect it separately. teams working mainly in [linear](/integrations/linear) can start with that issue review instead.

**one project and one decision are enough.** can we hand this off? what needs an answer? does the status note match the tasks?

a workspace-wide summary buries the wrong assumptions. compare the early reports with their tasks, then edit or pause the schedule in automations.

faq.q: what are people actually using an asana ai agent for?
faq.a: **try a check-in you already do by hand.** read prerequisites, compare status claims or collect unanswered contractor questions. these routines return review lists without editing tasks.

faq.q: can i use claude with asana without moving my tasks?
faq.a: **yes. the tasks stay in asana.** connect it and choose your bot's ai. switching ai keeps the bot's chats and memory.

faq.q: will the bot move deadlines without checking?
faq.a: **keep reviews read only to keep deadlines in place.** for a later editing job, limit the allowed actions and tell it to ask first. deadline edits do not automatically wait for approval.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

steps: connect asana read only for one bot
name the project and one task due tomorrow
ask what unfinished dependencies it has

mistakes.fix: ask for an unfinished prerequisite or a question, not a guess.

mistakes.mistake: allowing edits for a reading job
mistakes.fix: keep the first handoff review read only.

tip.text: a late task needs a reason, not another summary.
